content: Multi-account WhatsApp session isolation patterns (cross-checked, MEDIUM): production multi-tenant engines isolate per session/tenant — WaSphere uses per-workspace isolation, per-session API-key scopes, per-session proxy (HTTP/HTTPS/SOCKS5), sliding-window rate limit per session plus global throttle, HMAC-signed per-session webhooks with retries; wa-hub (whatsapp-web.js multi-tenant) keeps one isolated LocalAuth session dir per client id and explicit queue isolation (message queue and ensureReady() decoupled from lifecycle handlers; lifecycle handlers never await the queue or webhooks) to avoid cross-session stalls; whatsmeow deployments run one whatsmeow.Client per number with sqlstore (Postgres) so sessions survive restarts and migrate via pg_dump; Evolution API uses instances (one Baileys connection per instance) with per-instance webhooks, queues (RabbitMQ/Kafka/SQS) and S3 media storage. Failure modes to avoid: shared mutable store across accounts, one slow account's queue blocking others, mutating/deleting auth dirs while a client runs, and malformed app-state (chatModify) updates which log the account out of ALL devices.
